title: Fewest Tokens
hints: Try to answer the question for just the first i characters, for every i. How does the answer for i depend on shorter prefixes?
The last piece of the best split of the first i characters is some vocabulary piece ending at i. What would the rest of the split be?
best[i] = min over lengths len (1 to the longest piece) with s[i-len..i) in the vocabulary and best[i-len] reachable of best[i-len] + 1; best[0] = 0, and print -1 if best[n] is still unreachable.

wrong.greedy_longest.cpp: always takes the longest matching piece, which can strand the rest of the text
wrong.count_zero_start.cpp: initialises unreachable prefixes to 0 so they look free
wrong.tle_every_piece.cpp: tries every vocabulary piece at every position (fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: a text of up to 2*10^5 letters, up to 2000 pieces of length at most 8, minimise the number of pieces. Which plan fits?
options: At each position take the longest piece that matches
Recurse over every split without remembering results
Dynamic programming over prefixes: best[i] from best[i - len] for each piece length up to 8
Sort the pieces by length and apply them in turn
strategy.why: Greedy longest-first can strand the tail, so it is not optimal. Plain recursion revisits the same suffix exponentially often. Sorting pieces has nothing to do with order in the text. A prefix DP has n states and at most 8 transitions each, so it is O(n * 8) lookups.
